suggested_experiment_name: Black Hole Spin-Down Constraints from X-ray Binaries
notes: This is a theoretical paper on black hole superradiance of self-interacting scalar fields (axions). It does NOT present measured exclusion limits or observational data. Instead, it provides detailed theoretical calculations of how quartic self-interactions affect superradiant cloud dynamics around rotating black holes. The paper discusses observational signatures (gravitational waves, black hole spin-down, axion wave emission) and makes projections for future detection in experiments like Advanced LIGO and CASPEr-Wind, but does NOT extract or present numerical exclusion limit data points in the form of (mass, coupling) pairs. The paper is primarily theoretical/phenomenological, analyzing parameter space regimes (labeled A, B, C, D in Fig. 3) but not providing measured constraints. No coupling-vs-mass exclusion plot with extractable numerical data is presented. | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: Figure 10 shows constraints on axion parameter space (μ, f) from black hole spin measurements in X-ray binaries. The plot displays exclusion regions for different black hole systems (CVn X-1, GRS 1915+105, M33, GRO J1655-40, LMC X-1) as colored bands. The lower boundary of the exclusion region traces the minimum coupling strength required for superradiant instability to occur within the black hole's lifetime. The coupling plotted is g_an (axion-nucleon coupling), which is dimensionless. The x-axis represents axion mass μ in eV (log scale, range 1e-13 to 1e-11 eV), and the y-axis represents the coupling strength (log scale, range 1e-19 to 1e-10). The boundary shows a characteristic V-shaped profile with a minimum around 6-7×10^-13 eV, typical of superradiance constraints. The shaded regions above the boundary are excluded by observations of these black holes, which have not undergone the predicted spin-down. The paper discusses how self-interactions affect the superradiance growth and spin-down timescales, with implications for axion detection via gravitational waves and other observational signatures. | Calibration: Vision calibration: ×1e+1 (factor=1.00e+01, reason=spot-check verify/stage2, raw_ratio=31.25)
